newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Fresh mediation to end S.African truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Fresh mediation to end S.African truckers' strike.

text.p: South African trucking unions and employers were on Thursday locked in another round of mediation chaired by the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) in a bid to end a strike over wages.
"Another round of mediation kicked of at around 1100 GMT today (Thursday)," Road Freight Association chief executive Herman Lemmer told Reuters.
This follows a breakdown in mediation late on Wednesday night after the parties failed to find common ground.
Unions have been given a mandate to negotiate for a 14 percent across-the-board final demand, Transport and General Workers Union (TGWU) national organiser Thulani Dlamini said earlier.
"We tried to put something together that would amount to 14 percent and regulate current gaps between Gauteng and other regions at last (Wednesday) night's meeting," Dlamini said.

Road Freight Employer's Association chairman Johan van der Walt said in a statement on Thursday employers "remained flexible" to explore areas of settlement beyond the final offer of a wage increase between 10 to 15 percent.
The strike -- which started Wednesday morning -- has so far taken the form of pickets at companies which have resorted to employing scab labour in the industry.
It is the first in the sector in fifty years and also the first nationwide strike under the New Labour Relations Act which came into effect earlier this month.
